description: Provenance + regeneration parameters for the painterly tileset (see README.md)

tile_spec.hex: flat-top, point-to-point width 128 (2x render HEX_SIZE=32; drawn at 64 world px, crisp at MAX_ZOOM=2)
tile_spec.mask: hexgeom.hex_mask(128,128) core >128, dilated 1px (bleed) so abutting tiles overlap real content instead of AA fading

plains.gates: all 49 candidates passed luminance band 100-125 (measured 109-120); picks from a 23-candidate mutually seam-compatible clique (pre-v2 seam metric); truncation 0 fails

woods.class: object field (composited sprites; never swatch-cut - user: no cut-off canopies, trees end before the hex edge)

segmentation.connected_components: 8-neighbour, min area 400 px (prompt asked 6x6 grid but got 7 columns; components make the layout irrelevant)

compose.edge_inset: centre of crown must satisfy in_hex with shrink 2 + 0.72*max(w,h)/2 (no tree crosses the true hex edge)
compose.draw_order: sorted by y_base ascending (lower trees composite over higher)
compose.floor_discs: per tree, r=0.72*w at crown centre, rgba(30,44,26,185), gaussian blur 2, clipped to dilated mask
compose.placements: woods/placements.json (exact per-tree x, y_base, size, sprite index)

woods.ratified: 2026-07-01 via woods/review/woods-final-*.png ('sprites and layout are great' + packed density per 'can't really see much of the ground')

hills.class: whole-hex vignette (composited hill formations via vignette.py; swatch-cut texture REJECTED 2026-07-01: relief contrast breaks seams - best swatch's largest seam-compatible clique was 2/49 cuts vs plains' 23, and flatten.py can't help because the contrast IS the ridges, not illumination)

segmentation.foreground: min-channel distance from white > 25, alpha ramp (dist-25)*255/60
segmentation.discovery: downsample 8x (block max), hole-fill via border-connected background components, 4 largest clusters, row-major order
segmentation.interior: forced opaque (erode 2 at low res) so bright rock never goes transparent
segmentation.unmatte: partial-alpha edge pixels un-matted from white (kills the halo)

river.class: oriented texture (swatch-cut straight_v + straight_d + the four gentle-turn shapes + the fork_se_sw_s tributary junction; remaining fork orientations, ends and bridge still legacy PixelLab — later slices per ART_PIPELINE decision 4). Render-time L↔R mirror covers the other diagonal/turn orientations (see frontend riverTiles.ts, which also prunes junction-triangle adjacency artifacts so only the true junction hex renders a fork).
river.prompt: river/river-prompt-v7.txt (v4-v6 history: v4 good register but sandbars + curved edge entries; v7 bans sandbars outright and demands the course track the band's straights exactly)
style_refs: refs/ref_river_concept.png (creek register: narrow grey-teal water, concept-art crop)

layout_guide.note: node-straightened meander (river.py guide): straight vertical plateaus at every tile-period node, one sin^2 out-and-back lobe between - bends finish before the flat edges, so tiled columns never jerk at seams (user requirement 2026-07-02). Constant band width: a mid-lobe bulge in earlier guides invited per-bend sandbars.

river.generation_variance: NBP band-following is ~50/50 with no seed control; 3 of 6 rolls painted 150-250px braided rivers instead. Re-roll on failure; this swatch was roll 2 of the v7 prompt.

cut.note: 3:1 multi-scale cut (384px window LANCZOS-downscaled to the 128px tile) is the width control: the model overshoots the band ~1.5x, so cutting at 3x brings the water to 13-15 tile px. Side effect: river grass grain is finer than the 1:1-cut plains.

river.gates: river.py cut, tile px: crossing centre off <=3, top/bottom centre mismatch <=2, width mismatch <=4, width band 12-36, drift <=26, water half-span <=31, edge-straight dev <=2.5 over 18px spans; picks measured ct/cb <=0.9, water 13-15px, es <=1.8

recolor.note: hills-style grass-weighted HSV match toward the plains grass-core medians (recomputed from plains/picks, not hardcoded), with the sat ramp raised from hills' 0.12 so the desaturated water (sat ~0.21, hue ~90 - inside the hills weight!) keeps its ratified colour. Dropped worst angled seam 3.36->2.15 and dc step 15.8->6.9-9.4.

bridge.class: oriented deck-sprite composite (bridge.py): a slight-perspective bridge deck sprite (segmented from a white-background NBP deck sheet, the same white-sheet route as woods/city/hills - see vignette.py) + baked road ramps drawn to match the render-time vector road overlay + a soft contact shadow, all composited over a ratified painterly river base (frontend/src/board/tiles/river/*, archived at river/picks/). The composite preserves the base's own 1px-dilated hex alpha, so bridge tiles stay seam-compatible with river. The decks carry a little perspective lift (low railings, a shaded south front face), so the compositor NEVER rotates a sprite - rotating a perspective deck would swing its lit front face onto a side - and the sheet instead draws BOTH orientations natively (horizontal E-W decks and vertical N-S decks). Register per user direction: a strictly-top-down v1 round was rejected 2026-07-03 (placement bug + 'too top-down'); the v2 slight-perspective sheet was ratified. Only the two vertical turn tiles are applied so far; the remaining bridge orientations stay legacy PixelLab (later slices, per ART_PIPELINE decision 4).
bridge.prompt: bridge/deck-sprites-prompt-v2.txt (v2 = slight-perspective decks, ratified; bridge/deck-sprites-prompt-v1.txt = the strictly-top-down v1 round, rejected - prompt kept, its rejected-round sheets/sprites are not committed)

sheets.used_combined: bridge/sheets/deck-sheet-v2.png - the combined view the compositor segments: horizontal decks on the top row (from deck-sheet-v2-h-r2.png), vertical decks on the bottom row (from deck-sheet-v2-r1.png)
sheets.deck_sheet_vertical: bridge/sheets/deck-sheet-v2-r1.png - vertical N-S decks; the source row for the two applied turn tiles
sheets.deck_sheet_horizontal: bridge/sheets/deck-sheet-v2-h-r2.png - horizontal E-W decks; used only by the unratified straight_v (h-r1 was a rejected roll, not committed)
sheets.segmentation: segment_decks(): find_clusters -> 8 sprites, re-sorted deterministically (top-half-then-x) so index 0-3 = horizontal decks (wood_a wood_b stone_a stone_b), 4-7 = vertical decks (same order). Same white-sheet lift as the vignette terrains: softclip_above 135.0, factor 0.45, hole-filled interior, un-matted (build_vignette).

bridge.base_dir: river/picks (byte-identical to the applied frontend/src/board/tiles/river tiles)

deck.note: deck footprint = measured water span + 2*bank_px, at deck width_px (a touch wider than the 12px road so it shoulders past the ramps). Scaled from the native sprite with LANCZOS, never rotated. Position is derived, not stored: centred on the measured water crossing along the x=64 line.

bridge.water_gate: water_mask() classifies desaturated grey-teal water on hue 82-200 deg AND sat < 0.36, val 0.20-0.75 (the hue gate is load-bearing: warm low-sat tan/brown banks would otherwise mis-measure as water). measure_crossing scans a 3px strip at x=64 for the longest contiguous water run -> the deck span/centre.

road.note: baked ramps match the render-time vector road overlay (Board.tsx: 6 world px = 12 tile px, colour 0x6b4f2a). For the turn_ns shape they run straight from the n edge midpoint down through the deck to the s edge midpoint; the deck, composited on top, covers the join so the road appears to stop at the deck front face. Round-capped polylines; endpoints hit the edge midpoints exactly so neighbour road half-segments align.

noise.note: subtle seeded tonal noise on the ramp pixels (painterly softening); seed per tile

shadow.note: soft dark footprint just larger than the deck, under its long edges

bridge.placement_gate: After compositing, placement_gate asserts (1) along the x=64 crossing line every base-water pixel is covered by deck pixels (the deck must span the water - the v1 bug was a road crossing bare water) and (2) no road/ramp pixel remains visible on a former-water pixel; a failing tile raises PlacementError instead of being emitted. Both applied tiles pass.

Legacy 64px bridge art has no baked ramps and still gets the stubs.

road_nbp.class: NBP-finished painterly road tiles (ROADMAP Phase 8, Slice T5). Deterministic road composite (road.py flat ribbon over the ratified plains/hills bases) -> Nano-Banana-Pro image-to-image finish (wears the road into the ground / grades it over hill relief) -> deterministic post-chain (road-mask recolour to the ribbon palette + b08 rim blend) that tames NBP's width/colour freelancing and pins the grassy rim + crossings back to the deterministic input so tiles still abut invisibly. Auto-gated (drift/width/rim/lum/phantom); the user ratified the per-slot picks 2026-07-04. Plains fully covered (18 tiles); hills 6 tiles (straight_v is a width-waived near-miss, see gate_waiver). The four remaining hills shapes (turn_n_se, turn_ne_nw, end_ne, end_s) are deliberately left to the frontend vector road overlay (roadTiles.ts) — partial art coverage never breaks a road network. Render-time L<->R mirror covers the other orientations. Tool: scripts/tile-foundry/roadfinish.py.
road_nbp.sources: road/gens128/{tile} — committed 128px post-resize intermediates (raw 2K NBP gens under road/production/ are NOT committed). build replays the deterministic post-chain from these; regenerate with roadfinish.py export-sources.

geometry.note: input composite geometry (road.py); the deterministic flat ribbon the NBP finish repaints.

units.class: two-layer unit sprites (unit.py): each ratified NBP unit crop is split into a base layer (team-cobalt areas desaturated to grey, per-pixel value kept, 1px #14140f rim under-composited around the silhouette) and a tint-mask layer (RGB = value grey, alpha = soft team-area weight, no rim). The renderer multiplies the mask by playerColor and draws it over the base, so player colours scale to 32+ without baking any colour. Team areas are painted in a keyable cobalt (#3B5FC0 family, hue ~213-229 across all rounds); the classifier is a SOFT weight (feathered hue window x saturation ramp) so the base/mask boundary blends instead of haloing. All shipped sprites face WEST (native gen facing is east; every source carries mirror=true). Footprints ratified 2026-07-05: solid-bbox width 90px armor/artillery, 81px infantry ('downscale ~10%, it dwarfs the tank'), centred both axes on the 128 canvas, NO ground shadow. Tool: scripts/tile-foundry/unit.py.
units.sources: units/gens/extracted/ - committed un-matted RGBA crops of the ratified picks (the raw 2K gen sheets under units/gens/*.png are NOT committed, same reproducibility ruling as road/production/). build replays the full split from these.

rim.note: 0x14140f; base layer only, under-composited so AA edges darken into the outline instead of leaving a translucent halo

classify.note: weight = hue-window ramp x saturation ramp x alpha. Measured cobalt: hue 202.5-240 (p1-p99), highlight saturation bottoms out ~0.22 (tank p1); gunmetal/khaki sit below sat 0.14 or outside the hue window. Residue gate: no base pixel with hue 205-245, sat>0.25, v>0.12.

units.unmatte: partial-alpha AA pixels are un-matted against the mean RGB of the crop's alpha==0 pixels (the extractions kept coloured sheet-background bleed on their edges); gated against white fringe (v>0.85, s<0.15).
units.regenerate: python3 scripts/tile-foundry/unit.py build --manifest art/foundry/manifest.json --section units --out-dir <dir> [--verify frontend/src/board/units]; review montages: unit.py review --out-dir art/foundry/units/review
